name: image.steady2D
title: Image of a two-dimensional steady state

origin.description: Draws the state matrix the way image() does.
origin.usage: image(x, which = NULL, grid = NULL, add.contour = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: grid
arguments.text: A pair of x and y coordinates. The default runs from 0 to 1.

origin.details: The matrix is filled column-major. The first index is horizontal. A missing grid is seq(0, 1, length.out = n).
origin.value: A figure. The coordinates are the axes and the matrix.
origin.example:
g <- function(t, y, p) {
  Y <- matrix(y, nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  dY <- Y * 0
  for (i in 1:3) for (j in 1:3) {
    left <- if (i == 1) 0 else Y[i - 1, j]
    right <- if (i == 3) 1 else Y[i + 1, j]
    down <- if (j == 1) 0 else Y[i, j - 1]
    up <- if (j == 3) 0 else Y[i, j + 1]
    dY[i, j] <- left + right + down + up - 4 * Y[i, j]
  }
  list(as.vector(dY))
}
out <- steady.2D(y = rep(0.2, 9), func = g, dimens = c(3, 3))
image(out)

translation.description: Draws the state matrix the way image() does.

arguments.name: grid
arguments.text: A pair of x and y coordinates. The default runs from 0 to 1.

translation.details: The matrix is filled column-major. The first index is horizontal. A missing grid is seq(0, 1, length.out = n).
translation.value: A figure. The coordinates are the axes and the matrix.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from rootSolve import image_steady2d, steady_2d

def g(t, y, p):
    grid = np.asarray(list(y), dtype=float).reshape((3, 3), order="F")
    change = np.zeros_like(grid)
    for row in range(3):
        for col in range(3):
            left = 0.0 if row == 0 else grid[row - 1, col]
            right = 1.0 if row == 2 else grid[row + 1, col]
            down = 0.0 if col == 0 else grid[row, col - 1]
            up = 0.0 if col == 2 else grid[row, col + 1]
            change[row, col] = left + right + down + up - 4 * grid[row, col]
    return [change.reshape(-1, order="F")]

out = steady_2d([0.2] * 9, func=g, dimens=(3, 3))
image_steady2d(out)
